description.narrative:
The Capital Adequacy Frameworks (CAF) report, produced by a G20 expert panel, outlined how MDBs could reform their CAFs to increase their lending. It has become one of the key documents shaping thinking around the current World Bank evolution process. Publish What You Fund’s DFI Transparency Initiative, along with concurrent efforts to leverage GEMs data, are leading to a step change in the availability and quality of MDB (and bilateral DFI) investment data. This is important because while the CAF report highlights institutional level reform required to maximise the financing capacity of MDBs, there are also a series of investment level shifts required.
At the investment level, MDBs can increase their financing capacity through a combination of de-risking and mobilisation. By reducing third party exposure, either through the provision of first loss capital, technical assistance, or other means, MDB investments are more likely to attract co-financing from other, preferably private sector, sources. Progress has been made in disclosing data around the use of concessional finance, particularly through IFC’s disclosure of concessionality volumes in their blended finance operations. Better data around mobilisation is the logical next step in improving financial disclosure and improving the efficiency of DFI operations. We propose a two-pronged approach to improving mobilisation reporting: 1. Improve existing methods and 2. Introduce a new framework for reporting mobilisation for adoption by the leading DFIs who want to do more on this issue
